key_insight: IMPACT combines inverter-level cloud dynamics with plant history, solar geometry, and weather to improve 10–110-minute-ahead probabilistic photovoltaic power forecasts.
engineering_relevance: More accurate, calibrated PV forecasts could support short-term grid balancing, storage scheduling, and solar plant operations.
method: Four branches encode plant history, inverter dynamics via learned-adjacency graph attention, future solar geometry, and current weather.
Gated cross-attention fuses inputs; horizon-weighted cloud heterogeneity and inverter ramp-down signals enrich the geometry branch.
A decoder learns corrections to smart persistence, followed by online kernel-weighted adaptive conformal calibration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance above all 14 baselines, with FSS 0.2950—0.099 above the runner-up—and FSS 0.198 under overcast skies and 0.255 under variable skies; every branch contributed positively in ablation.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset size or cross-site validation, leaving generalization to other PV plants uncertain.
paper_title: IMPACT: Inverter-Informed Multimodal Learning for Photovoltaic Generation Forecasting
